search_log: Searched "The Last Thing He Told Me" "Laura Dave" excerpt and first chapter; found and inspected the authorized Serpent's Tail/Profile Books preview.
Searched "The Last Thing He Told Me" first person, point of view, narrator, and alternating point of view; found an explicit whole-book structural description from SparkNotes.

Searched for interior and ending passages involving Hannah, Bailey, Owen's note, and "When I finally allow myself to look up"; TIME and quote-study pages corroborated Hannah's first-person interior voice.
Checked the Simon & Schuster official title page; it verified the work but its catalog copy and reviews did not directly establish narrative person, so it was not used as person evidence.
Searches for epistolary, frame narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating narration produced no credible evidence of sustained base sections in another grammatical person.
person_note: The controlling narrator is Hannah Hall, a participant who narrates the investigation, her relationship with Owen, and her developing bond with Bailey as I. Numerous Goodreads event passages expose that voice across present action, memories, dialogue beats, and the late exhibition scene. Generic you/we aphorisms, attributed quotations, and character speech were treated as non-base rather than as second- or alternate-person narration. The authorized opening preview and explicit whole-book structural account agree on first person, and the research found no sustained competing narrator or person. The main limitation is that the Tier A excerpt covers the opening rather than the entire book, but the widely distributed quote evidence and whole-book description resolve that scope limitation.
